hero.title: 🗼 Wizard Tower Name Generator
hero.tagline: Arcane spires, necromancer towers, star observatories, ruins and wonky follies.

article.intro: A good wizard tower name tells you about the wizard before you knock: a jewel and a spire for a scholar (The Sapphire Needle of Mallowfell), bones and bells for a necromancer, a star tower for an astronomer. Every self-respecting mage needs a tower. This **wizard tower name generator** names arcane spires, grim necromancer towers, elemental towers, astronomers' observatories, ruins and eccentric follies, with a short description if you want one.

sections.heading: Eight good wizard tower names
sections.content:
All eight came from the generator, across its six styles:

  • The Sapphire Needle of Mallowfell: a jewel, a tall thin tower and a place: the classic arcane pattern.
  • Glimford Spire, whose door opens only to someone who speaks its true name: a scholar's tower with a puzzle at the front door.
  • The Spire of the Tolling Bell, whose master has not been seen alive for three centuries: a necromancer's tower that sounds like a warning.
  • Basaltcrag, carved into the side of a cliff, one room per century: an earth wizard's home that grew slowly.
  • Hepzibah's Meteor Tower, whose orrery holds a tiny, burning sun: an observatory named after the astronomer who built it.
  • The Ruined Tower of Broken Wands: a ruin that tells you how it ended.
  • Old Snorkle's Tower and Tea Room: a funny name for a wizard who has had to diversify.
  • The Biscuit Tower, whose wizard has been "just popping out" since last spring: a folly with a mystery in it.

sections.heading: How towers get their names
sections.content:
Towers have always been named for who built them or what they were for. Real ones show the pattern: Tycho Brahe's observatory on the island of Hven, built in the 1570s, was called Uraniborg, after Urania, the muse of astronomy. The follies that 18th-century landowners put up on their estates were named after the owner or the view. In fiction the wizard's tower became a type of its own, and Saruman's Orthanc at Isengard is the one most readers picture.

  • Arcane towers are needles, spires and pinnacles, often with a jewel or a colour: The Indigo Spire.
  • Necromancer towers take bones, graves and the names of the dead: The Tower of Ivo the Gravewalker, Dirgemere.
  • Elemental towers name their element: The Tower of Falling Hail, Blazetor.
  • Observatories watch the sky: Clearfell Observatory, The Comet Watch.
  • Ruined towers say what's left: The Roofless Tower of Wickby.
  • Funny towers belong to wizards whose neighbours have complained: Old Whiffle's Extremely Tall Tower.

Choose With a description for a line about the tower itself, which is often the best hook for a visit.

sections.heading: Using a tower in your story
sections.content:
• Name it after its owner if the wizard is still alive, and after its fate if they aren't.
  • Let the description set the quest: a door that opens to a true name means someone has to find that name.
  • Give each floor a purpose, from the library to the room nobody goes into.

For the wizard inside, try the Wizard Name Generator, and for where they trained, the Magic School Name Generator. For a tower that's become a prison, there's the Prison Name Generator, and for one that's fallen, the Ruins Name Generator.

For more, see all the world-building name generators.

faqs.question: What is a good name for a wizard tower?
faqs.answer: One that tells you about the wizard: The Sapphire Needle of Mallowfell for a scholar, The Spire of the Tolling Bell for a necromancer, or Hepzibah's Meteor Tower for an astronomer. Choose a style to match your wizard.

faqs.question: Can I get a description with the tower name?
faqs.answer: Yes. Choose With a description for a line about the tower, such as a door that only opens to its true name or a library that is bigger on the inside.

faqs.question: Are there funny wizard tower names?
faqs.answer: Yes. Choose Funny for names like Old Snorkle's Tower and Tea Room or The Biscuit Tower, whose wizard has been "just popping out" since last spring.
